newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire MPs quit Mobutu's parliamentary group.
newsitem.headline: Zaire MPs quit Mobutu's parliamentary group.

text.p: At least 100 Zaire lawmakers have quit President Mobutu Sese Seko's parliamentary alliance to join a new "nationalist" group, a spokesman said on Monday.
Although the founding members say they have formally renounced all collaboration with Mobutu, the common goal of the group appears to be to topple Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.

"We have already said that Kengo cannot guide the Zairean people into elections. He is an agent of Marshal Mobutu and his presence at the head of the government can only further electoral fraud in favour of the Marshal," Aziz Kumbi, spokesman for the new group told Reuters.
According to a list of members the new Parliamentary Nationalist Group comprises 344 MPs from all of Zaire's 11 provinces and from an official assembly total of 738 deputies.

Members of the group originate from all political tendencies including the radical UDPS opposition party of Etienne Tshisekedi, lawmakers from the president's Popular Movement party as well as some who remain ambiguously within Mobutu's FPC parliamentary alliance.
In theory Zaire's transitional parliament, in place since 1994, is divided into two so-called political families, that of the president and that of the opposition.
But the new alliance is attempting to transcend the two blocs, themselves bitterly divided.
Aziz said that the parliamentary nationalist group would mobilise the population in collaboration with a radical opposition alliance in order to block Kengo's government and force it from power.
"We do not support the UDPS but we share the same goal: to liberate the Zairean people, and we will participate in the same actions," Aziz said.
He said that were Kengo to remain prime minister at the time of elections scheduled to take place before July this year, the group would call for a total boycott.

Kengo's aides dismissed the new group as a fragile alliance of disgruntled politicians bitter at being excluded from the crisis government formed on December 24 to lead Zaire in a counter-offensive to recover territory seized by rebels.
